newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-MOORER SAYS BEAN IS IN OVER HIS HEAD.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-MOORER SAYS BEAN IS IN OVER HIS HEAD.

text.p: Michael Moorer says Vaughn Bean is in over his head in challenging for the International Boxing Federation heavyweight crown next month.

"He has to step up to my level, which he has never done before and I'm going to put him right back down to the level where he belongs," Moorer said Tuesday of Bean, whose 27-0 record has come against journeyman opposition.
"People who don't give him much of a chance know the type of fighter I am," Moorer said at a news conference officially announcing the fight between the two Americans on March 29 in Las Vegas.
"I'm on a totally different level than what he is," Moorer said of Bean, who is ranked only fifth by the IBF.

Moorer, 38-1, is a two-time champion, having defeated Evander Holyfield to win the title in 1994, only to lose it in his next fight, to George Foreman. He became champion again last year against German Axel Schulz and retained the crown by outpointing South African Francois Botha four months ago.
Moorer's trainer Teddy Atlas is not taking for granted that Bean's lack of top-level experience will guarantee victory for Moorer, but sees it as a huge disadvantage for the 23-year-old challenger.
"It's a big step up for him. It's like going from the wading pool to the ocean," Atlas said.
Bean, however, is not intimidated by taking on Moorer.
"This is my opportunity to show the world what I can do and I am going to do it," said Bean. "I am going to be heavyweight champion of the world. That I will be."
The only factor in Bean's favour is that Moorer may be looking past him and at the prospect of fighting the winner of the Mike Tyson-Holyfield rematch on May 3 later this year.
But Moorer says that will not happen.

"I have to focus on the task that is put in front of me at the time, which is Vaughn Bean," said Moorer. "Hopefully I'm successful that night, and after we will talk about anything that is presented to me after that."
Also on the card, former six-time champion Julio Cesar Chavez of Mexico, 98-2-1, will meet American Gary Kirkland, 28-1, in a non-title bout.

In two other title bouts, World Boxing Council strawweight champion Ricardo Lopez of Mexico, 44-0, will defend against Mongkol Lg Gym of Thailand, 17-1, and World Boxing Association junior middleweight champion Laurent Boudouani of France, 34-2, will defend against Carl Daniels, 38-2.
